text:
alex: Quick one — Python sampleapp under gunicorn + uvicorn: request_id shows up in logs but is redacted in traces. Seen across a few customers.

priya: That's odd. We normally redact PII at the log hook layer, but traces should carry a separate trace attribute. Can you paste the minimal stack?

alex: Using gunicorn with --worker-class uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker, app uses our middleware to set request_id from header X-Request-ID and puts it into opentelemetry baggage + logging context. Logs look like: 

INFO api.handler: user login req_id=[REDACTED] message="auth success"

but otel span shows attribute request_id: "req-7xk9" (raw). So logs redacted but traces not, which is backwards for GDPR concerns.

tom: Huh. Middleware ordering? If the log redaction runs after log formatting and we redact tokens there, traces might skip redaction because the span attribute was set before the redactor ran.

priya: We have two separate systems: our log redactor (runs in logging filter) and OTEL attribute sanitizer (runs in a span processor). They should both use the same redact rules, but configuration lives in two places right now. Bug: default redact list wasn't loaded into span processor for Python runtime in sampleapp.

alex: Repro snippet (very small):

```py
# middleware.py
from redwood_dx import set_request_context

def middleware(scope, receive, send):
    req_id = scope['headers'].get(b'x-request-id', b'').decode() or generate()
    set_request_context(req_id)  # sets logging context and baggage
    await app(scope, receive, send)
```

alex: Logging init code reads REDWOOD_REDACT_RULES from env and installs filter, span processor reads REDWOOD_REDACT_RULES_JSON but sampleapp sets only REDWOOD_REDACT_RULES. So mismatch.

priya: Oof. Config parity fail between logging hook and span processor. Should be unified. Two fixes: 1) SDK: single source of redact config (env key REDWOOD_REDACT) parsed by both hooks. 2) Provide migration shim in span processor to fallback to older env keys.

tom: Also saw gunicorn pre-fork hooks can mutate env for workers. If customers set REDWOOD_REDACT_RULES at runtime via config reload, worker neighborhoods can end up with different sanitizers. We should document that env-configs are snapshot at fork time.

alex: Any quick mitigation for current releases? Customers worried about traces leaking IDs.

priya: Two short-term options: a) Retroactive span sanitization: run a post-span hook that inspects attributes and redacts known patterns before export. b) Feature flag to instruct otel exporter to redact attributes matching the log redactor rules. Both doable. Retroactive sanitization safer.

infra-bot: ticket created: DE-4010 python span redaction mismatch (link: https://redwood.internal/DE-4010) :white_check_mark:

alex: I'll open a PR for: unify env var (REDWOOD_REDACT), add fallback mapping, and add a span processor unit test that ensures attribute redaction. Also will add a note in onboarding docs: "If you set redact rules via env and use gunicorn, ensure env is present in pre_fork or worker env."

priya: Please add an e2e in sampleapp that runs under gunicorn worker lifecycle (fork) and asserts both logs and spans redact the same sensitive tokens. Also add a small migration note for private customers.

tom: For SDK parity: mirror this change in Go and Node SDKs so REDWOOD_REDACT is consistent cross-runtime.

alex: Thanks — will send patch and link DE-4010. Also suggestion: add a lint in CI that checks logging and tracing configs are both reading the same env keys. Saves future drift.

priya: Agreed. Small follow-up: if anyone hits this in prod and needs an immediate kill-switch, set REDWOOD_ENFORCE_REDACT=1 in env; span processor will strip attributes matching default rules regardless of other config. Documented in the incident playbook.

alex: Great, thanks. Will include playbook note in PR. :shipit:
